title: 12th Parliamentary Election
subtitle: The January election returned the incumbent government amid an opposition boycott and rights-group criticism.
summary: Bangladesh held its 12th National Parliamentary Election on 7 January 2024. The Election Commission published official results, while major opposition boycott politics and rights-group reporting made the election's legitimacy sharply contested.
heroTagline: Formal results and political legitimacy moved in different directions.
whyItMatters: The election became a key prelude to the 2024 protest cycle because it deepened debates over participation, coercion, constitutional design, and democratic credibility.
longTermLegacy: Its long-term significance lies in how the January vote fed into later arguments about representation, legitimacy, and the conditions that preceded the July-August 2024 uprising.
identityMemoryNotes: The election is remembered differently by official result narratives and opposition or rights-based accounts of exclusion and repression.
